title: Waste and scrap of copper

review.classification: UNSD CPC 3.0 explanatory notes p. 204 list 39361 for copper waste and scrap. Neighbouring headings distinguish nickel and aluminium scrap. Page 203 distinguishes metal-bearing ashes and residues. New tube cutting offcuts retain their metallic tubular form and their origin and actual recovery-feed destination define the narrower product.
review.route_and_receiver: Swagelok distinguishes wheel cutting from sawing and identifies reaming. ReMA's Candy grade includes clean unalloyed uncoated tubing. Midland Metals describes collection of actual manufacturing scrap and clean tube offcuts. The separate Port Perry receiving guide accepts clean tubing without solder or fittings and documents distinct grades. None supplies a common lot, a default metal assay or an inventory factor.
review.measurement_and_allocation: Independently compared the two languages’ first-release denominator, accepted whole mass, separation of useful lengths and chips, burdened source tube, rejected/returned material, stock bridges and shared manufacturing burden allocation. Dispatch and post-release service keep the original cohort denominator. Actual evidence determines preparation and packaging.
review.identity_and_maturity: Verified the SHA-256 of the original Mass property and mass unit group against the independently checked archive. Each language carries 21 inventory rows. All 21 native exchange identities, including the reference product, still need compatible evidence. The targeted builder ran 108 measurement checks with zero skips. Twenty advisory range warnings remain. Scientific and translation review are pending.
